what: Several photo panels (on wide screens, two photos side by side per panel) are stacked in one spot and pinned to the screen. Scrolling down rolls the bottom edge of the top panel upward first (clip-path inset bottom 0→100%, one screen per panel, straight line, scrub .5), revealing the next panel. Section height is panel count × screen height. While the top edge of the section travels from 20% of the screen to the very top, the dark veil over the photo lifts from 1→0 in .1 steps, and it covers again while the bottom edge rises from the screen bottom to 80% (the veil follows at .3s ease). While inside <html> fx-stack-wipe-inside is attached to it and can hide the headline row

options.[data-fx-part=pin]: Group of panels pinned to the screen (sticky, 100vh)
options.[data-fx-part=item]: Overlapping photo boards — peeled away from the top in document order (the last board stays)
options.[data-fx-part=shot]: (if present) one photo each to be folded away instead of the panel on narrow screens — the two-photo panel on wide screens becomes one at a time on phones
options.[data-fx-part=overlay]: (If present) dark curtain that covers and lifts on enter and exit
options.narrow: Width in px at which it switches to shot, default 768
options.lag: Seconds of lag behind the scroll (scrub value), default .5

use: …

from.where: /  index.html .e-gallery (original .js-gallery-container — four panels, two-photo grid on wide screens, one photo at a time on phone)

note: Even if the stack of panels covers the full screen height, retraction follows scroll only (dragging is not blocked)
